items.c: Order of the small intestine segments

read.title: A tube with helpers
text: The digestive tract is one long tube, and its roots run in the same order food travels. Food enters the mouth (or/o, stomat/o), where the teeth (dent/i, odont/o), tongue (gloss/o, lingu/o) and saliva (sial/o) begin the work. It passes down the esophagus into the stomach (gastr/o), then into the small intestine, whose three parts are the duodenum, jejunum and ileum. The large intestine, most of which is the colon (col/o), absorbs water and ends at the rectum (proct/o, rect/o) and anus (an/o).

Three accessory organs pour secretions into the tract without food passing through them. The liver (hepat/o) makes bile, which the gallbladder (cholecyst/o, from chol/e for bile and cyst/o for sac) stores. The pancreas (pancreat/o) adds digestive enzymes.

Two pairs of look-alikes cause frequent errors. The ileum, part of the small intestine, is spelled with an e, while the ilium of the hip is spelled with an i. And -scopy terms name what the scope reaches: laparoscopy looks into the abdominal cavity, and esophagogastroduodenoscopy looks through the esophagus and stomach into the duodenum.

q.q: What are the three parts of the small intestine, in order?
How is the intestinal ileum spelled differently from the hip's ilium?
o: With an e instead of an i
